Checksum validation is what separates a real identifier from a number that
merely has the right shape. Each pair below is one value that passes its
checksum (must be detected) and one that matches the same regex but fails
the checksum (must be rejected). This is why the detectors carry validators
and not just length-based regexes.

Payment cards (Luhn):
  valid   payment card 4111 1111 1111 1111
  invalid payment card 4111 1111 1111 1112

IBAN (mod-97):
  valid   IBAN GB29 NWBK 6016 1331 9268 19
  invalid IBAN GB29 NWBK 6016 1331 9268 18

A second valid card for good measure: payment card 5555 5555 5555 4444.
An Amex that also passes Luhn: payment card 3782 822463 10005.

The invalid values above must survive un-redacted: the regex found them, the
validator threw them back.
